messages:
alerts-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT - streaming/generation p99 spike detected in us-west2-a. metric: p99_response_time = 4.6s over last 12m, p95 jumped from 420ms -> 1.1s. Affected path: continuous-batching (cont-batch) streaming. paging/evictions elevated. alert id: INC-1743219876
Priya S.: ACK. paging team paged. Starting triage: what changed in last hour? any deploys? any autoscale/placement events? :eyes:
Miguel R.: no deploys in last 2h. I see increased batch formation delay on a subset of workers: median batch_wait went from ~6ms -> ~60ms and batch sizes peaked at 28-32. Mixed seqlen workload spike (many short and very long requests) causing packing amplification + KV cache churn. logs show frequent KV evict and page faults on cont-batch GPU processes.
Eve L.: confirming traces — streaming stalls correlating with large batches that then do paging. This cont-batch path doesn't preempt streaming early enough. SLOs flagged for several customers (notably Acme Search).
Priya S.: immediate mitigation options: 1) reduce cont-batch max_batch to lower tail (quick flip) 2) enable preemptive-shedding for streaming so long requests don't block short ones 3) route high-seqlen traffic to fallback non-contbatch variant. Which is lowest risk?
Miguel R.: quickest is config flip to reduce max_batch and start preemptive-shed. We can do config via fleet-config and it takes ~30s to propogate. Fallback routing requires more safety checks.
Eve L.: agree. propose: set CONT_BATCH_MAX_SIZE=8 (was 32) and enable CONT_BATCH_PREEMPTIVE=true. Also temporarily increase streaming worker count on us-west2-a by +2 to absorb throughput while batch size is smaller.
Priya S.: do it. I'll run the commands.
Priya S.: ```
# apply quick mitigation
rdwctl config set contbatch.max_size 8 --region us-west2-a
rdwctl config set contbatch.preemptive true --region us-west2-a
rdwctl pool scale contbatch-usw2-a +2
```
ops-bot: queued change: contbatch.max_size -> 8 for region us-west2-a (change id: CHG-1743219884). Applying now.
ops-bot: change CHG-1743219884 applied successfully across 18/18 nodes. pool scale requested (scale id SCL-1743219885) - scaling started.
Miguel R.: seeing batch sizes drop on telemetry to median 6-9 within 45s. batch_wait back down to ~8ms. KV eviction rate decreasing.
alerts-bot: p99 response_time from streaming/generation now 1.05s (last 2m), p95 420ms. SLO still borderline but trending down.
Priya S.: customer impact check: Acme Search reported UI slowdowns 10:12-10:28 UTC, error spikes 3% for streaming endpoints. Customer success notified and we opened support ticket SUP-9821.
Eve L.: we should keep preemptive flag on and batch cap until traffic normalizes and we can tune scheduler fairness. Also need to capture a replay of mixed-seqlen requests for offline evals.
Miguel R.: action items: - create perf test with current seqlen mix (Miguel) - investigate scheduler fairness algorithm and whether we can bias packing to avoid amplifying long requests (Miguel/Eve) - evaluate adding a seqlen-based routing heuristic to route >1024 tokens to non-contbatch (Priya/Miguel)
Priya S.: creating follow-up ticket: INF-1743220001 with mitigation timeline, customer impact, and next steps. Linking dashboards: https://grafana.redwood/infx/streams?panel=latency&from=now-30m
Priya S.: Handoff summary for next oncall: mitigation applied (max_batch=8, preemptive_shed=true, +2 workers). Observed p99 drop from 4.6s -> ~1.0s. Customer Acme Search impacted (SUP-9821). Follow-ups: perf replay, scheduler fairness investigation, consider long-term routing for high-seqlen traffic, post-incident RCA.
next-oncall: taking over. Thanks all. I'll monitor for 60m and coordinate postmortem writeup. Please add any logs/notes to INF-1743220001. :thumbsup:
Priya S.: thanks team — I'll be available for any questions. Closing incident alert but keeping ticket open for RCA. :white_check_mark:
